title: Under-Nines
subject: a fourteen-year-old referee at a Sunday-morning under-nines football match on pitch three, shouted at by touchline dads in a league that keeps no score
caption: Nu-metal in the turn-of-the-millennium rap-metal style, as revived by mid-2020s nu-metal bands. Drop-tuned seven-string guitars chugging bouncy palm-muted riffs with dissonant high squeals; a slapped, clanky five-string bass locked to the kick drum; tight live drums with a hip-hop groove in the verses and double-kick in the choruses; a clean chorused guitar picking eerie harmonics under the pre-chorus. Dry, compressed, mid-heavy late-90s production. Male lead with rhythmic half-rapped verses, a tense sung pre-chorus and a full screamed chorus doubled by gang shouts. 96 BPM, D minor. Furious, funny, then sheepishly soft. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no EDM drops, no pop-punk, no orchestral strings.
lyrics:
[Intro - drop-tuned riff and live drums]

[Verse 1]
Sunday, nine a.m., pitch three, there's frost on the goal
I'm fourteen in a yellow shirt that swallows me whole
Fifteen quid in a sandwich bag, cash from the club
And a touchline full of dads in gilets gripping coffee cups

[Pre-Chorus - clean chorused guitar harmonics, tense sung]
Breathe in, count to ten
Little Alfie's sat down in the goalmouth again

[Chorus - screamed, gang shouts, double kick]
It's the under-nines, there's no table, there's no score
Sit back down in your camping chair
Fifteen quid and a whistle
I'm not paid enough for this, not paid enough for this

[Verse 2]
Steve in the gilet's screaming penalty down the line
He tripped on his own laces, Steve, he's eight, he's fine
His wife's got her phone up, filming me in portrait mode
Says it's going on the parents' WhatsApp before I get home

[Chorus - screamed, gang shouts, double kick]
It's the under-nines, there's no table, there's no score
Sit back down in your camping chair
Your lad's waving at a dog
He's not bothered, so why are you

[Bridge - half-time breakdown, gang vocals]
Final whistle, and the kids all shuffle into line
Fourteen sticky little hands, good game, ref, good game

[Chorus - half-time, clean chorused guitar, sung softly]
It's the under-nines, there's no table, there's no score
One of them hands me half his orange
And the whole touchline's gone quiet
I'm not paid enough for this, see you next week

[Outro - riff and feedback]
